workflows.name: In-Store Audio, Ambient Media & Customer-Experience Strategy

Automation Opportunity: - Footfall/dwell/basket attribution (VS-28); zone-based experience modeling; own-vs-partner decision support
Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: annual business case reviewed by CMO/CFO; channel-mix & zoning documented; capex via VS-40 gate
Cross-references: - links to VS-13 (CX), VS-14 (marketing/brand), VS-07 (store ops), VS-33 (strategy), VS-40/VS-112 (capex/PMO), VS-97 (real estate), VS-109/VS-37 (remodel/new-store); sets inputs for W4890–W4896
Pain Points / Risks: - **Strategic-invisibility risk**: Program cut if ambient-media uplift is unmeasured; mitigated by the footfall-to-basket KPI set (W4905)
- **Channel-overlap risk**: Undifferentiated music vs VS-48 retail-media vendor ads → cluttered, annoying store; mitigated by the channel-mix and zoning model
- **Format-mismatch risk**: Sensory identity not tuned to the big-box warehouse format and trade-pro customer; mitigated by brand-sound standards (W4890)
System Touchpoints: - FP&A/strategy (VS-33/VS-17.4); capex (VS-40/VS-112); analytics (VS-28); CX (VS-13); brand (VS-14); real estate (VS-97)

steps.activity: Set the in-store ambient-media strategy & operating model: the channel mix (background music, PA/paging, in-store digital signage, ambient scent), the brand-sound/sensory identity aligned to the "Your Home Building Partner" positioning, the zone-based experience (sales floor, lumber yard, contractor/pro lounge, customer-service counter, checkout, garden center), and the own-operate vs vendor-managed decision per channel

Build the strategic case: footfall/dwell/basket uplift evidence, brand-consistency across 200 stores, contractor/pro-experience differentiation (links VS-43/W1493), the opex/capex envelope, and KPIs (music-license compliance 100%, signage-uptime, footfall-to-basket attribution, CX/CSAT impact); sequence the multi-year roadmap into capex (VS-40) and the store-remodel/new-store programs (VS-109/VS-37)
Approve the program charter, operating budget, and governance (W4896); integrate into the marketing plan (VS-14), store-ops standards (VS-07), and the capex pipeline (VS-40/VS-112)

fields.Participants: Marketing (VS-14), Store Ops (VS-07), Commercial music provider (W4892)
fields.Trigger: Strategy set (W4889); seasonal calendar (VS-13.2/VS-64); brand refresh
fields.Volume: ~4–6 dayparts × ~12 months × group-wide standard applied to 200 stores

workflows.name: Background Music Programming, Playlist Strategy & Brand-Sound Standards

Automation Opportunity: - Daypart/zone auto-scheduling; clean-edit auto-filter; rotation-fatigue detection; seasonal-overlay auto-deployment
Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: brand-sound standard published; clean-edit + royalty-cover enforced; store-override limited & audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (brand), VS-07 (store ops/W4898), VS-137 (DAM/asset library), VS-63 (store comms), W4891 (royalty), W4892 (provider), W4908 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Licensing-gap risk**: A programmed track not covered by the license → infringement; mitigated by the royalty-coverage check (W4891)
- **Staff-fatigue risk**: Stale/repetitive playlists erode associate experience; mitigated by rotation cadence
- **Brand-inconsistency risk**: Stores self-programming → off-brand/mismatched music; mitigated by the published standard + audit
System Touchpoints: - Commercial music service/CMS (W4892); brand/digital-asset library (VS-137); store comms (VS-63); analytics (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~initial programming 3–4 weeks; ~ongoing 4–8 staff-hrs/month refresh; ~annual brand-sound review 1 week

steps.activity: Define the brand-sound standard: genre/mood/tempo/loudness by zone and daypart (e.g., upbeat morning, midafternoon trade-pro-leaning, calmer late-day), lyrics/clean-edit policy (family-friendly, no explicit content), Filipino/OPM content quota supporting local artists, and the playlist-rotation/refresh cadence to prevent staff fatigue

Program playlists via the commercial music service (W4892): build zone/daypart schedules, the seasonal/ber-months/event overlays (links VS-14/VS-64), the promo interstitials, and the licensed-vs-original music mix; verify all programmed tracks are royalty-covered (W4891)

Publish the standard to stores, train store managers on volume/override limits (links VS-07/W4898), and audit adherence (W4908); manage exceptions (regional/local-store events, contractor-lounge differ-entiation)
steps.r: In-Store Media Manager / Store Ops / Training

fields.Participants: FILSCAP & other PROs, Commercial music provider (W4892), Legal (VS-100), IP (VS-100.2), Internal Audit (VS-21)

workflows.name: Music Royalty Licensing — FILSCAP / OPM / IP Compliance & Statutory Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - Playlist-vs-license coverage auto-check; renewal-calendar auto-alert (VS-166); fee-area auto-calc from site master
Controls: - CTL-734: FILSCAP blanket license current for all 205 sites; playlist coverage verified before publish; renewal calendar tracked; audit-ready evidence
Cross-references: - links to RA 8293 (IP Code); VS-100/VS-100.2 (legal/IP), VS-15/VS-17 (AP), VS-21 (audit), VS-166 (license portfolio), W4890 (programming), W4892 (provider), W4908 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Infringement risk**: Unlicensed public performance → statutory damages per work + injunction (RA 8293); mitigated by the blanket license + coverage verification
- **Lapse risk**: A missed FILSCAP renewal leaves 200 stores unlicensed; mitigated by the renewal calendar (VS-166) + annual true-up
- **Double-coverage risk**: Paying both BuildRight-direct and via the music service for the same right; mitigated by the scoping step
System Touchpoints: - License/contract repository (VS-100.3/VS-166); AP/payment (VS-15/VS-17); playlist/CMS (W4892); legal/IP (VS-100.2); audit (VS-21)
Time Estimate: - ~initial licensing 2–4 weeks; ~annual renewal 3–5 days; ~continuous coverage verification absorbed into W4890 refresh

steps.activity: Identify all required music-public-performance licenses for public performance of copyrighted musical works and sound recordings in 200 stores under RA 8293 (IP Code): FILSCAP (Filipino + affiliated international societies for musical works), and the sound-recording/mechanical rights where applicable; scope per site-type and confirm the commercial music service's blanket-license coverage vs BuildRight's direct obligation

Obtain/maintain the licenses: complete the FILSCAP establishment survey (no. of sites, floor area, ambient vs featured use), negotiate the annual blanket license fee (typically area/no.-of-speakers-based), execute agreements, and pay; retain certificates and renewal calendar (links VS-166)

Verify ongoing compliance & statutory reporting: cross-check programmed playlists (W4890) against license coverage, submit any required music-use reports to FILSCAP/societies, manage the renewal calendar (W4889 of VS-166) to prevent lapse, and maintain the audit-ready evidence file for VS-21/internal-audit and any FILSCAP inspection (W4908)

fields.Trigger: Vendor model selected (W4889); contract expiry; expansion

workflows.name: Commercial Music Service / Background-Music Provider Selection & Contracting

Automation Opportunity: - RFP/scoring template; TPRM cyber-attestation integration (VS-161); contract-clause library (SLA/rights/DPA)
Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: licensed catalog + localization + offline + uptime SLA; rights-clearance allocation documented; TPRM DD + DPA; re-compete at term
Cross-references: - links to VS-03/VS-34 (procurement), VS-100.3 (contract), VS-161 (TPRM), VS-91 (privacy/DPA), VS-27.3 (cyber), VS-137 (DAM), W4890 (programming), W4891 (rights), W4910 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Rights-allocation risk**: Ambiguity on whether the service covers public-performance rights → BuildRight still infringes; mitigated by written rights-clearance allocation
- **Catalog-localization risk**: Weak OPM/Filipino/vernacular catalog → off-brand store; mitigated by the localization requirement
- **Offline-resilience risk**: Cloud-only music stops when a store network drops (VS-27); mitigated by local-cache/offline player
System Touchpoints: - Procurement/contract (VS-03/VS-34/VS-100.3); TPRM (VS-161); privacy/DPA (VS-91); cyber (VS-27.3); IT integration (VS-27); DAM (VS-137)

steps.activity: Define vendor requirements: licensed business-music catalog (clean-edit, OPM/Filipino content), zoned multi-channel delivery, central CMS/scheduling (W4890), dayparting, promo-interstitial insertion, in-store player hardware/software, offline resilience (store network outages per VS-27), uptime SLA, reporting/analytics, and the rights-clearance model (does the service's blanket license cover BuildRight's public performance, or is direct FILSCAP still required — W4891)

Run sourcing & contract: RFP, evaluate (catalog depth/localization/clean-edit coverage/commercial/uptime/TPRM cyber & financial DD VS-161), negotiate (term/exit/SLA/price-per-site/data-sharing RA 10173 VS-91), and contract via Legal with TPRM provisions; confirm the rights-clearance allocation in writing

Onboard: deploy the in-store player to 205 sites (W4896/W4906), integrate the CMS to the DAM (VS-137) and store-comms (VS-63), set the royalty/license hand-off with W4891, and manage performance (W4910) and re-compete at term

workflows.name: In-Store Digital Signage Content Strategy & Programming

Automation Opportunity: - CMS auto-scheduling/dayparting; promo-overlay auto-sync from VS-58; mandatory-content gating; stale-content auto-flag
Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: BuildRight-vs-vendor slot allocation; mandatory compliance content (PWD/price/safety) enforced; playback-audited
Cross-references: - links to VS-48 (retail media), VS-14 (marketing), VS-137 (DAM), VS-58/VS-64 (promotions), W4398 (wayfinding), VS-151 (price/tag), VS-85 (PWD discount), W4899 (publish), W4908 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Channel-conflict risk**: BuildRight content crowded out by VS-48 vendor ads → store feels like a billboard; mitigated by the slot-allocation policy
- **Compliance-content risk**: Missing mandatory PWD/senior-discount or price-integrity notices (RA 7394/RA 7277); mitigated by the mandatory-content checklist
- **Stale-content risk**: Outdated promo/price on screen → Consumer Act exposure + customer confusion; mitigated by the refresh cadence + audit
System Touchpoints: - Digital-signage CMS/player (VS-27/VS-113); DAM (VS-137); retail-media platform (VS-48); promotions (VS-58); safety/wayfinding (W4398); price/tag (VS-151); analytics (VS-28)
Time Estimate: - ~initial content strategy 3–4 weeks; ~ongoing 8–16 staff-hrs/week content production; ~campaign refresh per cycle

steps.activity: Define the BuildRight-owned signage content strategy distinct from VS-48 vendor-paid retail-media: brand/house content (welcome, category education, how-to, safety, wayfinding, price-integrity/RA 7394, PWD/senior discount notices VS-85), the BuildRight-vs-vendor-ad slot allocation, the screen zoning (entrance/aisle/checkout/pro-desk), and the content-production pipeline from the DAM (VS-137)
steps.r: Marketing Content / In-Store Media Manager / Retail Media

steps.activity: Program the signage playlist via the CMS (W4907/W4909): dayparting, promotional overlays (links VS-14/VS-58/VS-64), category-education loops, safety/wayfinding (links W4398), and the price/tag-compliance notices (links VS-151); coordinate the VS-48 vendor-ad slots so the two channels complement
steps.r: In-Store Media Manager / Retail Media / DAM

steps.activity: Localize & publish: Filipino/regional-language and store-specific content (links VS-14/W4903), schedule via W4899, and audit playback compliance (W4908/W4910); manage the content-asset library lifecycle in the DAM (VS-137)

fields.Participants: Marketing (VS-14), Store Ops (VS-07), Facilities (VS-138), HSE (VS-24), CX (VS-13)
fields.Trigger: Strategy set (W4889); pilot success; format refresh (VS-109)

Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: HSE sign-off (SDS/allergen); zone exclusion for chemical/garden aisles; pilot-gated rollout
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (brand), VS-138 (facilities/BMS), VS-24/VS-114 (HSE/SDS), VS-145 (garden), VS-13/VS-28 (CX/analytics), VS-35 (asset), W4906 (maintenance), W4910 (vendor)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Odor-clash risk**: A scent fighting paint/chemical/garden odors (VS-114/VS-145) → unpleasant store; mitigated by zone exclusion + intensity controls
- **Health-sensitivity risk**: Fragrance triggering customer/staff allergy/asthma; mitigated by HSE sign-off, mild/intensity-controlled formulas, opt-out
- **ROI-uncertainty risk**: Scent uplift hard to isolate; mitigated by the pilot-then-measure approach (W4905)
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/CAFM (VS-138); asset register (VS-35); CX/analytics (VS-13/VS-28); HSE/SDS (VS-24/VS-114); vendor (W4910)
Time Estimate: - ~pilot 4–8 weeks; ~ongoing maintenance absorbed into VS-138; ~annual review 1 week

steps.activity: Define the sensory/scent strategy & standards: the brand scent identity (consistent with the warehouse/home-building positioning, avoiding clash with paint/chemical/garden live-goods odors VS-114/VS-145), zone application (entrance, paint aisle exclusion, garden), intensity, and the own-vendor vs in-house model

Select the scent vendor/equipment, pilot at flagship/remodel sites (VS-109), and verify safety: SDS for fragrance oils (chemical-handling HSE VS-24/VS-114), indoor-air-quality/ventilation interaction (VS-138), and allergen/sensitivity considerations for customers and staff (RA 10173 health-data care); obtain HSE sign-off
steps.r: In-Store Media Manager / Vendor / HSE / Facilities

steps.activity: Roll out, operate, and measure: deploy dispensers, maintain via facilities (VS-138/W4906), track CX/CSAT and basket impact (W4905), and manage the vendor contract/SLA (W4910); retire if neutral/negative

workflows.name: In-Store Media Budget, Allowance & Vendor Co-Funding

Automation Opportunity: - Per-site allowance tracking; co-fund auto-recovery; CX-uplift attribution into FP&A
Controls: - CTL-734 (ensure controlled execution — In-Store Audio, Ambient Media Strategy & Music Royalty Compliance (PA-168.1).)
- CTL-734: annual budget approved by CFO/CMO; co-fund governed by slot-allocation policy; variance reviewed monthly
Cross-references: - links to VS-17.4/VS-33 (FP&A), VS-14 (marketing), VS-48/VS-39 (co-fund), VS-15 (AP), VS-40 (capex), W4905 (attribution)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-leakage risk**: Royalty/service/equipment spend untracked → opex creep; mitigated by the per-site allowance + P&L tracking
- **Co-fund-misuse risk**: Vendor co-fund distorting the BuildRight-vs-vendor slot balance (W4893); mitigated by the allocation policy
- **Budget-invisibility risk**: CX uplift not credited to the program → under-funded; mitigated by the P&L + attribution (W4905)

steps.activity: Build the annual in-store-media budget: royalty/license (W4891), commercial music service (W4892), signage content production (W4893), scent (W4894), AV equipment maintenance/refresh (W4906/W4910), and the per-site allowance; align to the marketing (VS-14) and capex (VS-40) plans

Pursue vendor co-funding: structure BuildRight-vs-vendor signage slot allocation (W4893) so VS-48 retail-media and category vendors co-fund screens/content (links VS-48/VS-39 co-op), recover the royalty/service cost, and document the revenue/co-fund in the retail-media P&L
steps.r: Retail Media / Finance / In-Store Media Manager

steps.activity: Track spend vs budget, manage variances, and report the in-store-media P&L (cost vs co-fund recovery vs CX uplift) into the marketing FP&A (VS-17.4) and corporate performance (VS-33.2)

workflows.name: Multi-Entity / Multi-Region Ambient Media Standards & Governance

Automation Opportunity: - Entity/regional compliance dashboard; centralized content-push to decentralized players; auto-chargeback (VS-72)
Controls: - CTL-734: group standards + variance approval matrix; centralized royalty/asset management; fair cost chargeback (VS-72)
Cross-references: - links to VS-14 (brand), VS-72 (shared services/chargeback), VS-63 (store comms), VS-100 (legal/entity), W4903 (localization), W4905/W4908 (analytics/audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fragmentation risk**: Each entity/region self-programming → brand erosion + duplicated licensing; mitigated by centralized governance
- **Localization-overreach risk**: Regional variance diluting the brand-sound; mitigated by the variance approval matrix
- **Cost-allocation risk**: In-store-media cost not fairly charged across 5 entities; mitigated by the VS-72 chargeback model
System Touchpoints: - Brand/standards (VS-14); shared services/chargeback (VS-72); store comms (VS-63); legal/entity (VS-100); analytics (VS-28)

steps.activity: Set the cross-entity ambient-media governance: group brand-sound/signage standards applied across the 5 entities (BuildRight Depot/Logistics/Digital Commerce/Property/Holdings), the entity-specific exceptions (DC will-call vs retail store vs HQ), the approval matrix for local-store/regional variance, and the centralized-vs-decentralized operating model

Manage multi-region localization & cultural variance: regional language/music preferences (Cebuano/Ilonggo/Bicolano/Waray/Tagalog, links W4903), local-store-event exceptions (barangay/fiesta, links W908/W1511), and consistent brand-sound while respecting regional identity
steps.r: Brand / Store Ops Regional / In-Store Media Manager

steps.activity: Govern via shared services (VS-72): central content/royalty/asset management with decentralized store execution, charge the in-store-media cost pool across entities (links VS-72), and report entity/regional compliance (W4908) and performance (W4905) to the group
steps.r: In-Store Media Manager / Shared Services / Finance
